fruits.extendedStory: He was sailing to conquer the island, the tale goes. Twice a year, on 2 February and 11 November, the morning sun shines through the great rose window. Its image lands on the wall right below the other rose window, and the two make a magic eight. Antoni Gaudí worked here too. Under the choir stalls he built a hollow space, so that singing would carry through the whole cathedral without microphones. It was found again about a hundred years later, during repairs.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Er war, so die Geschichte, unterwegs, um die Insel zu erobern. Zweimal im Jahr, am 2. Februar und am 11. November, scheint die Morgensonne durch die große Rosette. Ihr Bild fällt genau unter die andere Rosette an die Wand, und zusammen ergeben beide eine magische Acht. Auch Antoni Gaudí hat hier gearbeitet. Unter dem Chorgestühl baute er einen Hohlraum, damit sich der Gesang ohne Mikrofone in der ganzen Kathedrale ausbreitet. Erst rund hundert Jahre später entdeckte man ihn bei Reparaturen wieder.
localizedExtendedStory.en: He was sailing to conquer the island, the tale goes. Twice a year, on 2 February and 11 November, the morning sun shines through the great rose window. Its image lands on the wall right below the other rose window, and the two make a magic eight. Antoni Gaudí worked here too. Under the choir stalls he built a hollow space, so that singing would carry through the whole cathedral without microphones. It was found again about a hundred years later, during repairs.

localizedStory.de: Der Sage nach löst diese Kathedrale ein Gelübde ein. Im Sturm versprach König Jaume I. der Jungfrau einen Tempel, käme er heil an Land.
localizedStory.en: Legend says this cathedral keeps a vow. In a storm, they say, King Jaume I promised the Virgin a temple if he landed safely.

fruits.name: La Seu
fruits.story: Legend says this cathedral keeps a vow. In a storm, they say, King Jaume I promised the Virgin a temple if he landed safely.

fruits.extendedStory: The sculptor Antoni Campredon spent fifty days making the angel. Then he loaded it on a mule and took it to Sineu, to show King Jaume the Second. Sailing boats in the harbour once took their bearings from it. The tower has carried the angel's name since the 14th century. Down in the courtyard of arms, a white marble lion recalls the palace's Muslim past.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Bildhauer Antoni Campredon arbeitete fünfzig Tage an dem Engel. Dann lud er ihn auf ein Maultier und brachte ihn nach Sineu, um ihn König Jaume dem Zweiten zu zeigen. Segelboote im Hafen richteten sich einst nach ihm, und seit dem 14. Jahrhundert heißt der Turm nach dem Engel. Unten im Waffenhof erinnert ein weißer Marmorlöwe an die muslimische Vergangenheit des Palastes.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The sculptor Antoni Campredon spent fifty days making the angel. Then he loaded it on a mule and took it to Sineu, to show King Jaume the Second. Sailing boats in the harbour once took their bearings from it. The tower has carried the angel's name since the 14th century. Down in the courtyard of arms, a white marble lion recalls the palace's Muslim past.

localizedStory.de: Der Engel auf dem Palastturm dreht sich mit jedem Wind. Man sagt hier: Wer ständig seine Meinung ändert, ist wie der Engel vom Palast.
localizedStory.en: The angel on the palace tower turns with every wind. Locals say a person who keeps changing their mind is like the palace angel.

fruits.name: Palau de l'Almudaina
fruits.story: The angel on the palace tower turns with every wind. Locals say a person who keeps changing their mind is like the palace angel.

fruits.extendedStory: There are four of them, presiding over the hall under three huge chandeliers. Here members' daughters once made their debut in society. The building began in 1848 as a members' club, on the ground of a demolished convent. For a few years its hall even served as a public theatre, the Coliseo, with seats for nine hundred. For its opening session in 1983, the parliament had to meet in another building, the Llotja. The club building had not been bought yet.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Es sind vier, und sie wachen unter drei riesigen Kronleuchtern über den Saal. Hier gaben einst die Töchter der Mitglieder ihr Debüt in der Gesellschaft. Das Gebäude entstand ab 1848 als Mitgliederclub, auf dem Grund eines abgerissenen Klosters. Einige Jahre lang war sein Saal sogar ein öffentliches Theater, das Coliseo, mit neunhundert Plätzen. Zur Eröffnungssitzung 1983 musste das Parlament in ein anderes Gebäude ausweichen, die Llotja, denn der Club war noch nicht gekauft.
localizedExtendedStory.en: There are four of them, presiding over the hall under three huge chandeliers. Here members' daughters once made their debut in society. The building began in 1848 as a members' club, on the ground of a demolished convent. For a few years its hall even served as a public theatre, the Coliseo, with seats for nine hundred. For its opening session in 1983, the parliament had to meet in another building, the Llotja. The club building had not been bought yet.

localizedStory.de: Das Parlament der Inseln tagt in einem alten Ballsaal, dem Saal der Karyatiden, benannt nach gemeißelten Frauenfiguren. Mallorcas feine Gesellschaft feierte hier Galabälle.
localizedStory.en: The Balearic parliament debates in an old ballroom, the Hall of the Caryatids, named for its carved female figures. High society held gala balls here.

fruits.name: Parlament de les Illes Balears
fruits.story: The Balearic parliament debates in an old ballroom, the Hall of the Caryatids, named for its carved female figures. High society held gala balls here.

fruits.extendedStory: It is said to open a week before every other Christmas market in Palma. The square fills the ground of an old convent, with arcades running all the way round. A rare film from 1951 shows the city's food market here, its stalls lined up in rows in the middle. In the 1970s the whole square was dug out from end to end, to fit a four-storey car park underneath.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Er öffnet, heißt es, eine Woche vor allen anderen Weihnachtsmärkten in Palma. Der Platz liegt auf dem Grund eines alten Klosters, ringsum laufen Arkaden. Ein seltener Film von 1951 zeigt hier den Lebensmittelmarkt der Stadt, die Stände in Reihen mitten auf dem Platz. In den 1970er Jahren grub man den ganzen Platz von einem Ende zum anderen aus, für ein Parkhaus mit vier Etagen darunter.
localizedExtendedStory.en: It is said to open a week before every other Christmas market in Palma. The square fills the ground of an old convent, with arcades running all the way round. A rare film from 1951 shows the city's food market here, its stalls lined up in rows in the middle. In the 1970s the whole square was dug out from end to end, to fit a four-storey car park underneath.

localizedStory.de: Jede Weihnachten füllt der Markt von Santa Llúcia diesen Platz. Hier kaufen die Mallorquiner die kleinen handgemachten Tonfiguren für ihre Krippen.
localizedStory.en: Each Christmas the Santa Llúcia market fills this square. Mallorcans come for the little handmade clay figures of their nativity scenes.

fruits.name: Plaça Major
fruits.story: Each Christmas the Santa Llúcia market fills this square. Mallorcans come for the little handmade clay figures of their nativity scenes.

fruits.extendedStory: The fishmongers' open counters run one into the next for almost 80 metres. The market's name goes back to nuns known as the Monges de l'Olivar, after their earlier home near Esporles. Their convent in town was pulled down, and its ground became the square this market stands on. Some stalls are family affairs: one butcher's grandparents already had a stall at the old market on Plaça Major.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die offenen Fischtheken gehen fast 80 Meter lang ineinander über. Der Name stammt von Nonnen, die Monges de l'Olivar hießen, nach ihrem früheren Kloster bei Esporles. Ihr Kloster in der Stadt wurde abgerissen, und auf seinem Grund entstand der Platz, auf dem der Markt steht. Manche Stände sind Familiensache: Die Großeltern eines Metzgers hatten schon einen Stand auf dem alten Markt an der Plaça Major.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The fishmongers' open counters run one into the next for almost 80 metres. The market's name goes back to nuns known as the Monges de l'Olivar, after their earlier home near Esporles. Their convent in town was pulled down, and its ground became the square this market stands on. Some stalls are family affairs: one butcher's grandparents already had a stall at the old market on Plaça Major.

localizedStory.de: Kauf hier Fisch an einem Stand. Eine der Bars im Markt, heißt es, bereitet ihn dir zu, direkt von der Theke auf den Tisch.
localizedStory.en: Buy fish at a stall here. One of the market's bars, they say, will cook it for you, straight from the counter to the table.

fruits.name: Mercat de l'Olivar
fruits.story: Buy fish at a stall here. One of the market's bars, they say, will cook it for you, straight from the counter to the table.

fruits.extendedStory: Its roots reach so far that they have turned up in digs under La Rambla. The garden was once Palma's botanic garden, growing medicinal herbs for the pharmacy of the hospital next door. The house itself was a charity home. Rules printed in the 1940s show that it took in orphans and people who could not look after themselves. Everyone got up at seven, or half past seven in winter, and went to Mass. Then came the shoe, carpentry or printing workshops, or school.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Seine Wurzeln reichen so weit, dass man sie bei Grabungen unter der Rambla gefunden hat. Der Garten war einst Palmas botanischer Garten, mit Heilkräutern für die Apotheke des Spitals nebenan. Das Haus selbst war ein Wohltätigkeitshaus. Eine Hausordnung aus den 1940er Jahren zeigt, dass hier Waisen und Menschen lebten, die nicht für sich selbst sorgen konnten. Alle standen um sieben auf, im Winter um halb acht, und gingen zur Messe. Dann ging es in die Schuh-, Tischler- oder Druckwerkstatt oder zur Schule.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Its roots reach so far that they have turned up in digs under La Rambla. The garden was once Palma's botanic garden, growing medicinal herbs for the pharmacy of the hospital next door. The house itself was a charity home. Rules printed in the 1940s show that it took in orphans and people who could not look after themselves. Everyone got up at seven, or half past seven in winter, and went to Mass. Then came the shoe, carpentry or printing workshops, or school.

localizedStory.de: Im Garten der Misericòrdia wächst ein Ficus, dessen Krone 35 Meter misst. Er gilt als größter Baum Palmas.
localizedStory.en: In the Misericòrdia's garden grows a ficus with a crown 35 metres across. It is counted as the biggest tree in Palma.

fruits.name: La Misericòrdia
fruits.story: In the Misericòrdia's garden grows a ficus with a crown 35 metres across. It is counted as the biggest tree in Palma.

fruits.extendedStory: Today the Aljub is an exhibition room. The museum sits inside the Sant Pere bastion, a piece of the city walls from the late 16th century. It was so big and so well placed that one of Europe's most prestigious artillery schools was set up inside. When new owners wanted to build all over the site, Palma's people protested, and the bastion was protected as a historic ensemble.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Heute ist der Aljub ein Ausstellungsraum. Das Museum steckt in der Bastion Sant Pere, ein Stück der Stadtmauer aus dem späten 16. Jahrhundert. Sie war so groß und so gut gelegen, dass darin eine der angesehensten Artillerieschulen Europas eingerichtet wurde. Als neue Besitzer das ganze Gelände bebauen wollten, protestierten die Menschen in Palma, und die Bastion wurde als historisches Ensemble geschützt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Today the Aljub is an exhibition room. The museum sits inside the Sant Pere bastion, a piece of the city walls from the late 16th century. It was so big and so well placed that one of Europe's most prestigious artillery schools was set up inside. When new owners wanted to build all over the site, Palma's people protested, and the bastion was protected as a historic ensemble.

localizedStory.de: Unter dem Museum liegt der Aljub, eine Zisterne aus den 1640er Jahren. Erst Müllhalde, dann beim Bau des Museums wiederentdeckt.
localizedStory.en: Under the museum lies the Aljub, a cistern from the 1640s. Once a rubbish tip, it was found again while the museum was being built.

fruits.name: Es Baluard
fruits.story: Under the museum lies the Aljub, a cistern from the 1640s. Once a rubbish tip, it was found again while the museum was being built.

fruits.extendedStory: It was Jesus, the story goes, who had that door walled up, so that nobody would leave through it. The devil stormed off in a rage, they say, raising a gale as he went. Above the doorway, look for Mary standing on a crescent moon. Under her feet the devil is carved as an animal-like creature. The church was built for the Jesuits, on the site of the old Jewish synagogue.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Jesus selbst ließ die Tür zumauern, so die Geschichte, damit niemand durch sie hinausging. Der Teufel zog wütend ab, erzählt man, und entfachte dabei einen Sturm. Über dem Portal steht Maria auf einer Mondsichel. Unter ihren Füßen ist der Teufel als tierhaftes Wesen gemeißelt. Gebaut wurde die Kirche für die Jesuiten, auf dem Platz der alten jüdischen Synagoge.
localizedExtendedStory.en: It was Jesus, the story goes, who had that door walled up, so that nobody would leave through it. The devil stormed off in a rage, they say, raising a gale as he went. Above the doorway, look for Mary standing on a crescent moon. Under her feet the devil is carved as an animal-like creature. The church was built for the Jesuits, on the site of the old Jewish synagogue.

localizedStory.de: Der Sage nach war dem Teufel versprochen, wer die Seitentür nahm, und er lauerte hier. Sie wurde zugemauert, also schwor er, heißt es, ewigen Wind.
localizedStory.en: Legend says the devil was promised anyone using the side door, and waited here. It was walled up, so he swore endless wind here.

fruits.name: Monti-sion
fruits.story: Legend says the devil was promised anyone using the side door, and waited here. It was walled up, so he swore endless wind here.

fruits.extendedStory: The town hall clock is called En Figuera, after the bell-founder Pere Joan de Figuera. On New Year's Eve, thousands fill the square to count its last twelve strokes of the year together. A folk tale has Master Nadal stroll across this square and fall through a hole into a tunnel. He walks on and on, the tale goes, until he reaches a city under the ground. The gnarled olive tree here is reckoned to be 500 to 600 years old.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Rathausuhr heißt En Figuera, nach dem Glockengießer Pere Joan de Figuera. In der Silvesternacht füllen Tausende den Platz und zählen gemeinsam ihre letzten zwölf Schläge des Jahres. Ein Volksmärchen erzählt von Meister Nadal, der hier über den Platz spaziert und durch ein Loch in einen Tunnel fällt. Er geht immer weiter, so die Geschichte, bis er eine Stadt unter der Erde erreicht. Der knorrige Olivenbaum auf dem Platz soll 500 bis 600 Jahre alt sein.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The town hall clock is called En Figuera, after the bell-founder Pere Joan de Figuera. On New Year's Eve, thousands fill the square to count its last twelve strokes of the year together. A folk tale has Master Nadal stroll across this square and fall through a hole into a tunnel. He walks on and on, the tale goes, until he reaches a city under the ground. The gnarled olive tree here is reckoned to be 500 to 600 years old.

localizedStory.de: Such die Faulenzerbank an der Rathausfront. Man erzählt, hier sonnten sich Müßiggänger, statt zu arbeiten, und jede Ausrede begann mit „Wäre da nicht“.
localizedStory.en: Find the lazy man's bench on the town hall. Locals say idlers sunned here instead of working, every excuse starting 'if it weren't for'.

fruits.name: Plaça de Cort
